title: The Charity Envelope
subtitle: Four hundred and eighty pounds vanished. A seal and a paper trail tell another story.

consultation.speaker: Benny
consultation.text: The donation box was empty after the courthouse fundraiser. They think I took the money.

consultation.speaker: Oliver
consultation.text: Who last checked the box, and who was authorised to empty it?

consultation.speaker: Benny
consultation.text: I sold the hot dogs. Brick handled security. Milo says the box was empty at half past four.

consultation.speaker: Oliver
consultation.text: We will check that time, the keys, and the collection trail. Nobody is guilty because they stood near a box.

opening.speaker: Bumble
opening.text: This court takes charity money seriously. The decorative collection box has already retained counsel.

opening.speaker: Victor
opening.text: An empty box, a borrowed key, and a vendor with pockets. The prosecution sees a pattern.

opening.speaker: Oliver
opening.text: A pattern is useful when its pieces belong to the same facts. Let us check them.

opening.speaker: Bumble
opening.text: Milo, start with your last observation of the collection box.

evidence.title: Fundraiser photograph
evidence.description: 16:35. The original event photograph shows sealed charity envelope C17 inside the transparent collection box.
evidence.inspection: The camera timestamp is 16:35 and the blue C17 seal is visible through the box. This disproves the claim that the box stayed empty from 16:30 until 17:00.

evidence.title: Signed donation ledger
evidence.description: The volunteers counted 480 pounds and sealed it in envelope C17 at 16:25. Two volunteers signed the ledger.
evidence.inspection: Amount, envelope ID and seal number belong together: 480 pounds in C17. Any later receipt must match both the amount and the intact seal.

evidence.title: Cash collection policy
evidence.description: Security must collect sealed donations at 16:40 and use the night-deposit safe. Vendors may not handle donation-box keys.
evidence.inspection: An empty display box after the scheduled collection is expected. The money is meant to move into the secure deposit system, not remain on display.

evidence.title: Borrowed-key register
evidence.description: Benny borrowed K4 at 16:10 and returned it at 16:45. K4 opens the catering cupboard. D2 remained with Officer Brick.
evidence.inspection: The alleged borrowed key cannot open the donation box. The register distinguishes K4, the catering cupboard key, from D2, the donation-box key.

evidence.title: Night-safe deposit receipt
evidence.description: 16:43. Officer Brick deposited sealed envelope C17. The safe issued receipt N204. The collection entry was filed under security, not catering.
evidence.inspection: The same envelope ID and intact blue seal link the photographed money to a secure deposit before the 17:00 missing-money report.

evidence.title: Bank return: envelope C17
evidence.description: Next morning, the bank opened C17 from deposit N204 and counted 480 pounds. The seal was intact on arrival.
evidence.inspection: The bank count matches the volunteers' ledger exactly. The funds were secured and accounted for; an empty display box was mistaken for a theft.

statements.text: The box stayed empty from 16:30 until my 17:00 report.
statements.press: MILO: I looked at the table. I may have remembered the wrong photograph.

statements.text: The missing-money report was made at 17:00.
statements.press: MILO: I reported an empty box. I did not ask whether collection had happened.

statements.text: The donations had been sealed before the stalls closed.
statements.press: MILO: Two volunteers counted them and used a blue seal.

resolution.speaker: Oliver
resolution.text: The original 16:35 photograph shows envelope C17 still inside the box. Your claim that it stayed empty is contradicted by the photograph.

resolution.speaker: Milo
resolution.text: Then my missing money was a missing timestamp.

resolution.speaker: Brick
resolution.text: I have the key register. Every borrowed key has its own lock listed.

resolution.speaker: Victor
resolution.text: Then let us discuss the key in the defendant's possession.

statements.text: Benny borrowed a courthouse key that afternoon.
statements.press: VICTOR: Signed out at sixteen ten. At last, a signature that is not mine.

statements.text: That borrowed key opened the donation box.
statements.press: VICTOR: It is marked K4. I did not consider that the number might matter.

statements.text: The collection policy reserves donation handling for security.
statements.press: BRICK: The donation-box key is D2. I kept it on my duty ring.

resolution.speaker: Oliver
resolution.text: K4 opens the catering cupboard. D2 opens the donation box and remained with Brick. Your keys do not match.

resolution.speaker: Brick
resolution.text: I collected C17 at sixteen forty under the policy. The receipt was filed in security.

resolution.speaker: Bumble
resolution.text: Enter the night-safe receipt and the bank confirmation. Trace the actual envelope.

resolution.speaker: Benny
resolution.text: I borrowed a cupboard key to retrieve napkins. My most dangerous equipment is absorbent.

statements.text: By 17:00 the display box was empty.
statements.press: MILO: That observation is correct. The inference is having a difficult afternoon.

statements.text: The donation ledger records 480 pounds in envelope C17.
statements.press: MILO: The blue seal was intact when the volunteers finished.

statements.text: No authorised collection occurred before my 17:00 report.
statements.press: MILO: I checked the catering folder. OLIVER: Where does security file its receipts?

resolution.speaker: Oliver
resolution.text: Receipt N204 records Brick depositing intact C17 at 16:43, seventeen minutes before your report.

resolution.speaker: Brick
resolution.text: The bank counted four hundred and eighty pounds. Same envelope. Same seal. Full amount.

resolution.speaker: Bumble
resolution.text: The box was empty because its contents were safely collected. Give the court the complete chain.

closing_prompt: Connect the photograph, the different keys, receipt N204 and the bank count. Where did the donations go?
conclusions: Benny emptied the box with K4 and returned the money anonymously.
Brick collected sealed C17 under policy. The night-safe receipt and bank count account for all 480 pounds.
The 16:35 photograph proves the box was empty at 16:30.

verdict.speaker: Bumble
verdict.text: The money was present at 16:35. Benny's key could not open the box. The authorised deposit and bank count account for every pound.

verdict.speaker: Bumble
verdict.text: On the charge of stealing the charity donations: NOT GUILTY!

verdict.speaker: Benny
verdict.text: Can the charity keep the interest? I have been paying in anxiety.

verdict.speaker: Milo
verdict.text: I have added a new line to my checklist: ask security.

verdict.speaker: Oliver
verdict.text: Follow the actual money. A nearby pocket is not a chain of custody.

verdict.speaker: Brick
verdict.text: Receipt filed. Case closed. Napkins returned.
